title: Gayoom wins fourth consecutive uncontested presidential referendum
reason: No presidential referendum was held in 1990. Gayoom's term sequence ran: 1978 (1st), 1983 (2nd), 1988 (3rd), 1993 (4th), 1998 (5th), 2003 (6th). A 1990 referendum is fabricated; the nearest real referendum was 1988 (3rd term) or 1993 (4th term). The event year drifts >2yr from any real Gayoom referendum.

title: Journalist Mohamed Nasheed arrested after criticizing Gayoom regime
reason: Nasheed helped establish the political magazine Sangu in 1990 and was arrested for an article alleging the government rigged the 1989 elections. He was named an Amnesty International prisoner of conscience in 1991 and sentenced to 3 years in April 1992. The arrest occurred in the 1990-1991 window, within ±2yr of the curated year.

title: Gayoom wins fifth presidential term amid deepening authoritarian rule
reason: A presidential referendum was held in October 1993 in which Gayoom won 92.76% as the sole candidate. Note: this was his 4th term (not 5th — the 5th was in 1998); however the event year 1993 is accurate and the core fact of an uncontested referendum win is real. HRW and Amnesty documented systematic repression throughout this period.

title: Tourism sector surpasses fishing as dominant GDP contributor
reason: By 1992 tourism had definitively overtaken fishing as the top earner; by the mid-1990s it was the dominant GDP contributor. Tourist arrivals grew at ~10% annually through the decade. The curated year of 1995 is consistent with well-documented economic data showing tourism dominance was established in the early-to-mid 1990s.

title: Gayoom wins sixth presidential referendum
reason: A presidential referendum was held in October 1998 with Gayoom winning 90.9% as sole candidate. Note: this was his 5th term (not 6th — the 6th was in 2003); however the event year 1998 is accurate and the uncontested referendum is a verified fact. The term-number label is incorrect but the underlying event is real.

title: Severe coral bleaching devastates Maldivian reef ecosystems
reason: The 1997-1998 El Nino triggered mass coral bleaching across the Indian Ocean. Live hard coral cover on shallow Maldivian reefs fell from ~70% to under 8% after the 1998 event, with 60-100% coral mortality reported depending on species and locality. Multiple peer-reviewed studies confirm this as one of the worst bleaching events on record.

title: Evan Naseem killed in prison custody, triggering anti-government riots
reason: Hassan Evan Naseem was beaten to death by NSS personnel at Maafushi Jail on 19 September 2003. The killing sparked mass protests in Male on 20-21 September; prison guards shot three more inmates (killing Abdulla Ameen, Ahmed Shiyam, and Ali Aslam) and injured 17. Gayoom declared a state of emergency. Event is precisely documented.

title: Gayoom declares state of emergency after Male riots
reason: Following Evan Naseem's death and the Male civil unrest of September 20-21 2003, Gayoom declared the first state of emergency in Maldivian history. Security forces cracked down on protesters. Multiple sources including Wikipedia and Amnesty International confirm this event and date.

title: Maldivian Democratic Party founded in exile
reason: The MDP was founded on 10 November 2003 by Mohamed Nasheed and Mohamed Latheef in self-exile in Sri Lanka and the United Kingdom, following the September 2003 unrest. It became the first structured opposition party in Maldivian history, confirmed by Wikipedia and Britannica.

title: Gayoom permits multi-party system under domestic and international pressure
reason: In June 2004 Gayoom presented wide-ranging reform proposals to parliament including allowing political parties, under pressure from the MDP and international community. The formal legalization came in June 2005 when parliament unanimously voted to recognize parties. The 2004 date is within ±2yr of the actual legalization and reflects when Gayoom announced the reforms.

title: Indian Ocean tsunami kills 82 and devastates two-thirds of inhabited islands
reason: The December 26 2004 tsunami killed 82 people and left 24 missing in the Maldives. Nearly all 199 inhabited islands were affected. Economic losses were estimated at approximately $460-470 million, roughly 62% of GDP. Two-thirds of Male was flooded. Data confirmed by Wikipedia and World Bank-ADB joint assessment.

title: People's Majlis votes to allow multi-party elections
reason: On 2 June 2005 the Maldivian parliament (People's Majlis) voted unanimously to legally recognize political parties and allow multi-party elections, a pivotal democratic reform. This paved the way for the 2008 constitution and competitive presidential election. Event date and details confirmed by IPU Parline and Wikipedia.

title: Constitutional referendum approves presidential system
reason: A constitutional referendum was held on 18 August 2007 in which 62% of voters chose a presidential system over a parliamentary alternative supported by the MDP. Gayoom backed the presidential system. The result laid the groundwork for the 2008 constitution, confirmed by Wikipedia's 2007 Maldivian constitutional referendum article.

title: New democratic constitution ratified with bill of rights
reason: Maldives' sixth constitution was completed in June 2008 and ratified by President Gayoom on 7 August 2008. It introduced the first bill of rights, separation of powers, an independent judiciary, and paved the way for the October 2008 multi-party presidential election. Confirmed by Constitution of the Maldives Wikipedia and IDEA.

title: Nasheed defeats Gayoom in first multi-party presidential election
reason: Mohamed Nasheed (MDP) won the October 28 2008 presidential runoff against Gayoom with 54.25% vs 45.75%, ending 30 years of Gayoom rule in the first competitive multi-party election. Gayoom conceded; peaceful transfer of power occurred on 11 November 2008. Confirmed by Wikipedia and Al Jazeera.

title: Cabinet holds underwater meeting to highlight climate threat
reason: On 17 October 2009 President Nasheed and 13 ministers held an underwater cabinet meeting at 6 metres depth in a lagoon off Girifushi island, signing a resolution calling for global carbon emission cuts. The declaration was presented at Copenhagen COP15 in December 2009. Widely covered by CNN, NBC, CBC, France 24.

title: Nasheed announces plan to make Maldives carbon-neutral within a decade
reason: In 2009 President Nasheed announced a plan for the Maldives to become the world's first carbon-neutral country by 2020, through wind turbines, solar panels, and a biomass plant. He also publicly raised the possibility of purchasing land abroad (India, Sri Lanka, Australia) if sea levels continued to rise. Confirmed by Climate Action and UN News.

title: Opposition protests erupt over economic grievances and judicial disputes
reason: Large-scale protests began in May 2011 over economic mismanagement and rising commodity prices, escalating through late 2011 with religious framing added by the opposition alliance. The judicial crisis — Nasheed's arrest of Criminal Court Chief Justice Abdulla Mohamed in January 2012 — grew directly from this 2011 protest period. Confirmed by Wikipedia 2011-2013 Maldives political crisis article.

title: Nasheed forced to resign after police mutiny and military pressure
reason: On 7 February 2012 Nasheed resigned after police defied government orders and joined protesters, and military also refused to disperse the crowd. Vice President Waheed was immediately sworn in. Nasheed called it a coup; the Commonwealth could not conclusively determine constitutionality. The core event — forced resignation under police mutiny — is confirmed by NBC News, Al Jazeera, Time Magazine.

title: Supreme Court annuls first round of presidential election
reason: The Maldives Supreme Court annulled the September 7 2013 first-round results (in which Nasheed led with ~45%) on 27 September 2013, citing allegations of ineligible voters in a 4-3 decision. International observers had deemed the election free and fair. Event confirmed by Al Jazeera and IFES Election Guide.

title: Abdulla Yameen wins disputed presidential election
reason: Abdulla Yameen (PPM), half-brother of Gayoom, won the re-run presidential second round in November 2013 with approximately 51% of the vote, defeating Nasheed. Yameen was inaugurated on 17 November 2013. The prolonged judicial annulment process raised democratic concerns widely reported by international media and Wikipedia.

title: Yameen consolidates power and curtails press freedom
reason: HRW's August 2018 report 'An All-Out Assault on Democracy' documents Yameen tightening control over state institutions, restricting media freedoms, and harassing independent outlets from 2014 onward, including the disappearance of journalist Ahmed Rilwan in August 2014. Regulatory constraints on civil society are also documented by Civicus Monitor.

title: Nasheed convicted of terrorism and sentenced to 13 years in prison
reason: On 13 March 2015 Nasheed was convicted under the Anti-Terrorism Act for ordering the arrest of Criminal Court Judge Abdulla Mohamed while president, and sentenced to 13 years at Maafushi Prison. Amnesty International called it 'a travesty of justice.' US State Dept expressed concern. The Supreme Court overturned the conviction in November 2018.

title: China-Maldives free trade agreement negotiations launched under Yameen
reason: China-Maldives FTA negotiations began in December 2015 under President Yameen, went through five rounds, and concluded in September 2017 before being signed on 7 December 2017. The 2015 launch date is accurate. The FTA was the first bilateral FTA for the Maldives and China's 16th FTA. Confirmed by China Ministry of Commerce and multiple sources.

title: Nasheed granted political asylum in the United Kingdom
reason: Nasheed was allowed to travel to Britain for surgery in January 2016 and granted political asylum in May 2016. He continued to lead the MDP opposition from UK exile. Confirmed by Wikipedia's Mohamed Nasheed article and multiple news reports.

title: China-Maldives Friendship Bridge opens connecting Male to Hulhumale
reason: The Sinamalé (China-Maldives Friendship Bridge) officially opened on 30 August 2018, not 2017. Construction began in 2016 and was completed in 2018. The year in the curated record is off by one year but within the ±2yr tolerance. Total cost was approximately USD 200-210 million (Chinese grant ~USD 116-126M plus loan). It is the first inter-island bridge in the Maldives.

title: Yameen declares state of emergency and arrests Supreme Court justices
reason: On 5 February 2018 President Yameen declared a 15-day state of emergency after the Supreme Court ordered release of political prisoners. Security forces stormed the Supreme Court, arresting Chief Justice Abdulla Saeed and judge Ali Hamid. Former President Gayoom was also arrested. The UN condemned the action. Confirmed by NPR, Al Jazeera, CNN, and Wikipedia.

title: Ibrahim Mohamed Solih defeats Yameen in presidential election
reason: Opposition candidate Ibrahim Mohamed Solih won 58.3% vs Yameen's ~41.7% in the September 23 2018 presidential election. Yameen conceded. Solih was inaugurated on 17 November 2018, marking a democratic restoration. Most international observers declined the government's invitation but the result was widely recognized as legitimate.

title: Supreme Court overturns Nasheed's terrorism conviction
reason: On 26 November 2018 the Maldivian Supreme Court vacated Nasheed's 13-year terrorism sentence, ruling he had been wrongfully charged and the case should not have gone to trial. Nasheed returned from exile in November 2018 and was later elected Speaker of the People's Majlis in May 2019. Confirmed by Al Jazeera and Maldives Independent.

title: Solih government pivots foreign policy toward India
reason: President Solih adopted an 'India First' policy from taking office in November 2018, signing defense cooperation agreements and accepting Indian military personnel to operate gifted helicopters and a Dornier surveillance aircraft. India provided development aid as a counterweight to Chinese BRI projects. Confirmed by ORF and Carnegie Endowment analyses.

title: Yameen convicted of money laundering and sentenced to five years
reason: In November 2019 the Maldivian Criminal Court found Yameen guilty of money laundering related to a USD 1 million transaction from SOF Pvt Ltd (linked to the MVR 3.3 billion MMPRC embezzlement scandal) and sentenced him to five years and a USD 5 million fine. The Supreme Court later overturned this conviction in November 2021. Confirmed by Maldives Independent and Euronews.

title: COVID-19 border closure devastates tourism-dependent economy
reason: The Maldives closed borders in March 2020 and reopened on July 15, 2020. GDP contracted by approximately 33.5% in 2020, with Q2 2020 seeing a year-on-year decline of 51.6%. Over 45,000 tourism workers were affected. Government revenue was severely reduced. Confirmed by PMC article, World Bank, and UNDP assessment.

title: Nasheed survives assassination attempt by IED blast in Male
reason: On 6 May 2021 a remotely detonated IED (packed under a motorcycle seat with ball bearings) exploded near Nasheed's home in Male, critically injuring him. He underwent 16 hours of surgery. Police attributed the attack to Islamist religious extremists. Four men were charged with terrorism. Confirmed by Wikipedia and HRW.

title: Tourism rebounds to 1.3 million arrivals after pandemic collapse
reason: The Maldives recorded 1.3 million tourist arrivals in 2021, recovering from a pandemic low of 555,494 in 2020. The one-millionth tourist was welcomed in late October 2021. India and Russia were the leading source markets. The rapid rebound is confirmed by the World Bank Maldives Development Update and Visit Maldives data.

title: Yameen sentenced to 11 years for resort island bribery and embezzlement
reason: On 25 December 2022 the Maldivian Criminal Court sentenced Yameen to 11 years in prison and a USD 5 million fine for bribery and money laundering related to the lease of V. Aarah island for resort development to parliamentarian Yusuf Naeem. The conviction barred him from the 2023 presidential race. Confirmed by OCCRP and Times of Addu.

title: Mohamed Muizzu wins presidency on India Out platform
reason: Male Mayor Mohamed Muizzu (PNC) won the September 30 2023 presidential runoff with 54.06% of the vote, defeating incumbent Solih (39% first round). His campaign centred on the 'India Out' movement demanding removal of Indian military personnel. The result marked a sharp foreign policy realignment confirmed by Al Jazeera and The Diplomat.

title: Muizzu formally requests withdrawal of Indian military personnel
reason: The day after being sworn in (November 18 2023), President Muizzu formally requested India withdraw approximately 77-89 military personnel operating gifted aircraft. India agreed on December 3 2023; troops departed in stages before May 10 2024. Confirmed by VOA News, The Defense Post, and Al Jazeera.

title: Muizzu signs 20 agreements with China during state visit to Beijing
reason: During Muizzu's January 8-12 2024 state visit to Beijing, 20 bilateral agreements were signed covering infrastructure, tourism, blue economy, digital economy, BRI projects, fisheries, and social housing. China upgraded the bilateral relationship to a 'comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership.' Confirmed by Al Jazeera and the Maldives President's Office.

title: Maldives signs defense agreement with China as Indian troops depart
reason: On 5 March 2024 the Maldivian Defense Ministry signed a free military assistance pact with China. Indian troop withdrawal began by March 10 and was completed by May 10 2024. The simultaneous Chinese military engagement and Indian departure is confirmed by CNN, Al Jazeera, and Bloomberg.

title: PNC wins parliamentary supermajority consolidating Muizzu's mandate
reason: In the April 21 2024 parliamentary elections, Muizzu's People's National Congress won 66 of 93 seats, securing a supermajority sufficient to amend the constitution. With aligned independents the total reached 72-73 seats. MDP collapsed to 12 seats. Confirmed by The Diplomat, Wikipedia, and IFES.

title: Debt-to-GDP ratio reaches 115 percent amid fiscal crisis warnings
reason: Multiple 2024 sources confirm the Maldives public debt-to-GDP ratio was approximately 110-115% in 2024, with external debt service obligations of over $500M in 2025 and ~$1.07B in 2026. China is the largest creditor (owed ~$1.3B); India provided a USD 400M currency swap in October 2024 after Muizzu moderated his anti-India stance. ORF and IMF confirm the fiscal distress.
